title: Claude Code 2.1.219: Claude Opus 5 added as default Opus model, 1M context
raw_text: Added Claude Opus 5 (claude-opus-5) as the new default Opus model with 1M context window (expanded from previous limits); Fast mode pricing: $10/$50 per Mtok. Removed Opus 4.7 from fast mode; /fast now applies to Opus 5 and Opus 4.8.
affected_capability: Claude Opus 5 - 1M token context window, new default Opus model
practical_impact_note: Directly affects any Discovery Lab or Dinev Assistant workflow using Claude Code/Agent SDK with Opus - larger context window and a new fast-mode pricing tier are available immediately, no migration required.

source_name: Tech Press Roundup (Axios/9to5Mac/TechCrunch, via search synthesis)
title: Anthropic releases new model, Opus 5
raw_text: Claude Opus 5 comes close to the frontier intelligence of Claude Fable 5 at half the price. Opus 5 approaches the capabilities of Claude Fable 5 across many tasks, while costing $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens, the same price as the prior Opus model release, Opus 4.8. Opus 5 is Anthropic's fourth Claude 5 model release in less than two months.
affected_capability: Claude Opus 5 - near-Fable-5 capability at lower cost
practical_impact_note: Note: this source's standard-mode pricing ($5/$25 per Mtok) differs from Claude Code Changelog's fast-mode pricing ($10/$50 per Mtok) for the same model - both quotes are preserved verbatim rather than reconciled, per this tool's own Evidence Discipline; a human should confirm which pricing applies to which usage mode.

title: Anthropic updates Claude voice mode with more capable models
raw_text: Claude expanded voice mode with Opus and Sonnet, connected tool actions, and support for many more languages. Voice mode now runs on Claude Opus, Claude Sonnet, and Claude Haiku.
affected_capability: Claude voice mode - expanded model support and connected tool actions
practical_impact_note: Relevant to Dinev Assistant if it uses or could use Claude's voice mode - tool actions during voice sessions are new.

title: MCP 2026-07-28 Specification Release Candidate: stateless protocol architecture
raw_text: The initialize/initialized handshake is eliminated, and the Mcp-Session-Id header and the protocol-level session that came with it are also removed. This enables a plain round-robin load balancer to handle traffic without sticky sessions or shared session stores. Roots, Sampling, and Logging are deprecated, with at least twelve months between deprecation and the earliest possible removal. Release candidate locked May 21, 2026; final specification July 28, 2026.
affected_capability: MCP specification goes stateless - session handshake removed, extensions framework introduced
practical_impact_note: Directly relevant to Discovery Lab's own MCP usage and any future scheduled/multi-instance deployment of Observation Agent-style tools over MCP. 12-month deprecation window means no urgent migration action; worth a WATCH note for when the final spec ships July 28, 2026 (3 days after this capture).

title: Model Context Protocol prepares to break with its stateful past
raw_text: The new protocol revision goes stateless, removing the initialize handshake and the protocol-level session. Features formally marked as deprecated will remain functional for at least 12 months.
practical_impact_note: Independent corroboration of the primary MCP blog announcement (should cluster with it, not stand alone).

title: Google releases three new Gemini models - but no 3.5 Pro
raw_text: Gemini 3.6 Flash is Google's workhorse model that promises improved capabilities in coding, knowledge work, and multimodal performance while reducing token usage by up to 17%, making it cheaper than its predecessor 3.5 Flash. Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite is the most cost-effective model in the class, and 3.5 Flash Cyber is a specialized model fine-tuned for finding and fixing cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
affected_capability: Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber released
practical_impact_note: 3.5 Flash Cyber (a cybersecurity-specialized model) is directly relevant to Trust Engine's audit/verification workstreams; Gemini 3.5 Pro remains delayed, which is itself worth a WATCH note.

title: Evaluating Memory in LLM Agents via Incremental Multi-Turn Interactions
raw_text: This paper identifies four core competencies essential for memory agents: accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding, and selective forgetting. Recent benchmarks for LLM agents primarily focus on reasoning, planning, and execution, while memory is under-evaluated due to lack of benchmarks.
